m:sjohn: Open Monday to Saturday from 9am to 4:45pm, last entry at 4pm (cathedral website). On Sundays and public holidays it's closed to visitors. Ticket €15 for adults, with audio guide; prices and hours on stjohnscocathedral.com. Shoulders and knees must be covered.
m:palace: Ticket €12 for adults (Heritage Malta): reduced €10 for young people and over-60s, €8 for children. Exact hours not read (Heritage Malta's pages show them as an image): generally open every day, but to be confirmed on heritagemalta.mt. The Throne Room is closed until further notice. The State Rooms stay closed until 1:30pm on 28 October, 18 November and 2 December 2026, and all day on 26 October 2026; the Armoury is open on those days too. Closed on 24, 25 and 31 December, 1 January and Good Friday.
m:manoel: Tour times and price not checked: see the theatre's website (teatrumanoel.mt) and book online. Tours don't run when there are rehearsals or performances.
m:barrakka: The garden is open every day from 7am to 10pm and entry is free. The panoramic lift down to harbour level costs €1 (return), open from 7am to 9pm from November to May. The Saluting Battery is open every day from 10am to 5pm; the cannon is fired at noon (with a short commentary from 11:45am) and at 4pm. Entry to the battery is paid (price not read, see salutingbattery.com). Closed at Christmas, New Year, Good Friday, Easter and 15 August.
m:lascaris: Open Monday to Saturday from 9:30am to 5:30pm, last entry at 5pm; it doesn't appear to open on Sundays. Adult ticket (from age 16) €20, reduced €19 for over-60s, children €7. Guided tours at 10:30am and 12:30pm for €5 extra. Card only; best to buy your ticket online (lascariswarrooms.com).
m:elmo: Open every day from 9am to 5pm from October to March (last entry 4:30pm), from 9am to 6pm from April to September. Adult ticket €10, reduced €7.50 for young people, over-60s and students, €5.50 for children (6–11). The First World War section is closed until further notice. Closed on 24, 25 and 31 December, 1 January and Good Friday.
m:gate: Free to walk, at all hours. The kiosk of fried date pastries (imqaret) under the gate is open every day from 8am to 10pm (hours from guides, to be confirmed). Parliament can only be visited on free guided tours by booking (times to be checked on the Parliament website: not read).
m:strait: Free to walk. By day it's quiet and life shifts to the evening; venues change hands often, so check hours case by case.
m:hastings: A public garden, free entry. Opening hours not checked.
m:birgu: The ferry leaves from the quay below the Upper Barrakka Gardens (Lascaris Wharf), also reachable with the panoramic lift (€1): a ride costs about €2 per person (price from 2026 guides, to be confirmed). The ferries aren't part of the bus network and aren't covered by the Explore card. After 7:30pm prices go up (about €3.50). Fort St Angelo and the Birgu museums have their own hours, not checked.
vd:cordina: Valletta's historic café, open since 1837, on the square in front of the library: breakfast, pastizzi, pastries and quick lunches at the outdoor tables. It's a place to sit, not to rush.
vp:cordina: Breakfast €8–15; a pastizz costs about €1.50 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:lot61: A small, bright café on Republic Street, with breakfasts, eggs, toast and brunch dishes made with local produce. Good for a lighter start to the day than usual.
vp:lot61: Breakfast or brunch €10–18 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:society: A café on a side street a short walk from St John's, with breakfasts, sandwiches and cakes. Pleasant even in the rain.
vp:society: Breakfast €8–14 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:bridge: The bar-restaurant near the Upper Barrakka Gardens, with a terrace and a view of the Grand Harbour: breakfast until noon, then sandwiches, salads and hot dishes. You choose it for the view more than the menu.
vp:bridge: Breakfast €10–16 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:sphinx: A pastizzi counter, the little filo pastries with ricotta or peas: eaten standing, hot, with a tea or coffee. It's the cheapest and most Maltese lunch in the city.
vp:sphinx: A pastizz costs about €0.50–1 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:museumcafe: A lunch café where you get Maltese ftira, a flatbread with tuna, capers, olives and onion, or a sandwich. It closes early and doesn't open on Sundays.
vp:museumcafe: A ftira costs about €4–8 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:aaron: A restaurant of home-style Maltese cooking: between September and December there's lampuki pie, the seasonal fish baked in pastry, and stews. Closed on Sundays.
vp:aaron: A main course costs about €20–30 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:doffice: A bistro a few steps from the Grandmaster's Palace, with braġioli (beef olives) and other Maltese dishes, at lunch too and with no afternoon break.
vp:doffice: A main course costs about €18–26 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:kiosk: The kiosk under the city gate where they fry imqaret, date-filled pastries: hot, greasy and delicious, to eat as you walk into the city.
vp:kiosk: A few pieces cost €1–2 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
cd:fortangelo: The Knights' fortress in Birgu, with a view over the Grand Harbour.
cx:fortangelo: Reached by ferry from Valletta or by taxi.
cd:muza: The national art museum, in the Auberge d'Italie.
cd:archeologia: The Venus of Malta and finds from the megalithic temples.
cd:hagarqim: Two megalithic temples, older than the pyramids, on the coast.
cx:hagarqim: It's about 14 km from Valletta: you need a car or a bus.
cd:ipogeo: An underground temple from 3000 BC, with limited entry.
cx:ipogeo: There are very few places: book weeks in advance.
cd:portocruise: An hour by boat among the fortresses, with Birgu and Senglea.
cd:roccapiccola: A noble family's palace, still lived in, with an air-raid shelter.
cd:inquisitore: The Inquisition's tribunal in Birgu, with its cells.
